statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-52968: when an application passes a URL to xdg-open, the browser it starts treats the request as a user-initiated navigation and sends SameSite=Strict cookies, which can help a cross-site request forgery (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2025/06/23/1). The CVE record is tagged disputed, and Debian rates it unimportant as a hardening issue rather than a security issue in xdg-utils (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-52968). The xdg-utils project has published neither a fix nor a statement on it; the reporter's suggested mitigation first needs browsers to offer a way to open a URL as untrusted, which xdg-open could then pass on. The xdg-utils package currently published for Debian 13, a rebuild of Debian 1.2.1-2, ships xdg-open 1.2.1 without any such option. Open question: whether xdg-utils upstream rules this behaviour out of scope for xdg-utils, or browsers and xdg-utils ship the untrusted-launch support; this owner stays under investigation until one of those happens.
